title: Scaled matrix-vector accumulation
summary: Recovered VA 0x4385f0 (RVA 0x385f0), 252 bytes, as a genuine thiscall member with a partial object layout. Reads a three-float vector, computes each padded matrix row as ((rowY*y)+(rowX*x))+(rowZ*z), multiplies by the corresponding scale, and adds to the three accumulator fields. Only offsets 0x140 through 0x14b are written. Direct caller 0x438815 supplies a stack-local difference-of-products vector; original class name and physical meanings are unresolved. Original instructions were checked directly against Game.exe and the accepted oracle bytes compared equal. This is readable behavioral recovery, not a matching rebuild.
test_description: GCC i386 freestanding harness calls the accepted original at 0x4385f0 with thiscall ABI and the recovered member. 16384 comparisons cover four rounding modes, four FTZ/DAZ combinations, 256 edge/random fixtures, and external vector plus aliases into accumulator, matrix, and scale. Edge fixtures include signed zero, subnormal limits, finite extremes, infinities, quiet/signaling NaNs, identity and cancellation-order assertions. Compares finite/non-NaN output bits and quiet-NaN classification, full MXCSR status/control, all object bytes outside the three outputs, surrounding guards, and external input preservation. Installs initialized test-owned FS backing and checks head restoration after every oracle call. Accepted oracle bytes compare equal with original executable. Local GCC test passes; pinned VS2013 compiles implementation at O1, O2, and O2 /Oy-.
known_limits: Partial object view ends at 0x224; original class identity, full size, field names and physical units are not established.
NaN payload and sign selection when multiple NaNs participate are not specified by portable C++; tests require quiet-NaN classification rather than payload identity.
Floating-point exceptions are masked in tests. Trapping exception timing, invalid pointers, concurrent mutation and Windows exception dispatch are outside validation.

Arithmetic assumes scalar float rounding without reassociation or fused operations, as in the supplied GCC flags. Native MSVC compilation is compatibility evidence, not native behavioral or byte-matching validation.
